ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the upper left is the brain, the lower left is the spinal cord, and the right side is muscle. Inside the muscle, two structures, a and b, are labeled; b is located in the muscle effector part and is innervated by a pathway from motor neurons in the spinal cord; a is connected to a nerve fiber returning to the spinal cord, and the arrow in the question is marked near this nerve fiber leading from the muscle sensory structure to the spinal cord. Then reason: the nerve fiber at the arrow belongs to the afferent feedback pathway in reflex regulation, can transmit muscle state information into the spinal cord, and promotes excitation of the motor neurons that innervate b. If this nerve fiber is cut at the arrow, afferent feedback decreases, the excitation of the motor neurons that innervate b weakens, so the contraction strength of structure b will weaken.
